added_failure_basis: the reviewed run is a diagnostic node with no test arms: its manifest carries no baseline_suite and no after_suite block, and its test_logs name diagnostic gate logs (compare.log, cpu-stages.log, gpu-stages.log, cpu-krylov.log) rather than suite arms; with no readable arm there is no added failure id to derive, so the count is 0 over an empty id list, not a measured zero over a failing pair
findings: docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/certificate-300-device-carrier.html:70 blocking: the mechanism for the 11-coordinate difference is described as an exact-float64-equality dedup, but nova/equilibrium/stencil_mesh.py:395 (sample_lookup) and nova/equilibrium/separatrix_clip.py:139-140 (_point_key) both quantise with np.rint(point / tolerance) at a bin width of about 7e-14 m, so vertices agree when they land in the same bin, not because they are bit-identical; nova/equilibrium/stencil_mesh.py:349 sets atomic.tolerance to 128*eps*scale, roughly ten times finer than the ~7e-13 m cell jitter the same page measures, which is why 11 merges flip; consequently repair site 1 at certificate-300-device-carrier.html:141 proposes to replace an exact-equality merge that does not exist with an integer key that is already there, and names the function but no line, so a repair node following it would look for code that is not present; the correct repair is to widen the quantisation bin (the tolerance handed to np.rint) beyond the jitter, at stencil_mesh.py:395 and separatrix_clip.py:139

docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/certificate-300-device-carrier.html:118 non-blocking: cell 103 is characterised as an ordinary complete hexagon with area 8.411e-3 m2, rank 89 of 340 by area and flagged regular, but no log or json in the run directory carries that census, so the conclusion that the singularity is not a degenerate or clipped cell rests on an unrecorded probe; only the index 103 is evidenced, at cpu-normalisation.log:5

scripts/certificate_300_carrier/trace_krylov_action.py:261 non-blocking: main prints EXIT=0 unconditionally, as does scripts/certificate_300_carrier/compare_carrier_stages.py:198, and the recorded cpu-krylov.log carries two STAGE_FAILED lines for normalised_current_moments and current_moment_image, so a partially failed run is filed with a clean exit and the receipt cannot distinguish a complete run from a partial one
